data.title: Reading International Earnings Call Signals Strong Recovery
data.description:
Reading International ((RDI)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Reading International’s earnings call was strongly constructive, led by sharp year-over-year gains in revenue, cinema profitability, EBITDA, earnings per share, food and beverage spending, membership and debt reduction. However, low cash, a remaining nine-month loss, weaker U.S. real estate and theater results, higher costs, below-pre-pandemic attendance and ongoing legal matters remained important risks.

Revenue Growth Accelerates

Reading International’s third-quarter 2026 revenue rose $13.1 million, or 25%, to $65.3 million. Strong performances from Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey, along with a stronger Australian dollar, drove the improvement.

Nine-Month Revenue Improves

Revenue for the first nine months increased $24.6 million to $177.3 million. Higher attendance in Australia and the U.S., supported by a stronger film slate and a 9.8% rise in the Australian dollar, contributed to the gain.

Net Loss Narrows

Third-quarter net income reached $0.5 million, compared with a $4.2 million loss a year earlier, while earnings per share improved to $0.02 from a $0.18 loss. The nine-month net loss fell 53% to $5.4 million, and loss per share improved to $0.24 from $0.51.

Operating Profit and EBITDA Surge

Global operating income rose to $6.1 million from a $0.3 million loss in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 158% to $9.2 million, while nine-month adjusted EBITDA increased $6.9 million to $19.7 million.

Best Recent Third-Quarter Metrics

Cinema segment operating income reached $8.3 million, Reading’s best third-quarter result since 2018. Overall operating income, net income and basic earnings per share also reached their strongest third-quarter levels in several years.

Broad Cinema Revenue Gains

Global cinema revenue increased 28% to $61.9 million. Australian revenue rose 39% to $28.5 million, U.S. revenue climbed 19%, and New Zealand revenue advanced 22% to $3.6 million.

International Cinema Profitability Improves

Australian cinema operating income increased 161% to $4.8 million from $1.8 million. New Zealand moved from breakeven to $0.4 million, while average ticket prices reached functional-currency records of $17.03 in Australia and $15.35 in New Zealand.

U.S. Cinema Turns Higher

U.S. cinema revenue rose 19% despite the closure of 10 screens at California Reading Cinema. Operating income improved from breakeven to $3.1 million, showing stronger results even with a smaller screen footprint.

Valley Plaza Renovation Pays Off

Following its renovation, Valley Plaza’s cinema generated 62% higher total revenue in the third quarter. The project added a TITAN LUXE screen, Dolby Atmos, luxury recliners and other upgrades, while improved film availability also supported the result.

Food and Beverage Spending Sets Records

Food and beverage spending per patron reached quarterly records in every market: $9.31 in the U.S., $8.70 in Australia and $7.48 in New Zealand. U.S. spending exceeded comparable figures reported by Cinemark and AMC and increased 3.8% sequentially.

Membership Programs Expand

Australia and New Zealand rewards membership exceeded 745,000, with paid memberships above 57,000. U.S. free and paid memberships exceeded 52,000 and approached 2,800, respectively, while Angelika’s U.S. program had about 200,000 members.

Investment in the Cinema Experience

Reading continued upgrading seats, luxury recliners, premium large-format screens, food and beverage programs, Dolby Cinemas and Dolby Vision and Atmos installations. The company also introduced 26 Colossal screens, adding to eight TITAN LUXE auditoriums and one IMAX auditorium.

New Zealand Expansion Plans

Reading plans to take over the Dunedin cinema formerly operated by the Rialto Cinema joint venture and relaunch it as the company’s first Angelika site in New Zealand. A major Wellington renovation is also planned, including premium screens, Gold Lounge auditoriums, upgraded food and beverage offerings and a higher-end lobby.

Debt Reduction and Liquidity

Net debt fell to about $153.4 million, the lowest level since 2018. Reading repaid $19.1 million to Valley National Bank and $5.2 million to Bank of America, extended the 44 Union Square loan and refinanced a $6.2 million Santander loan with a new $7 million facility.

Refinancing Adds Cash

The ConnectOne refinancing carries a 7.125% interest rate and a 25-year amortization schedule. It includes monthly payments of about $50,000 and generated approximately $700,000 in additional unrestricted cash after costs.

Real Estate Sale Supports Balance Sheet

Reading sold the Cinemas 1, 2 and 3 property on October 30, 2026, for $41 million. Proceeds funded debt repayment, an $8 million collateral deposit for 44 Union Square, operating payables, cinema rent and upcoming capital expenditures.

Australian Real Estate Performs Well

Australian real estate revenue increased 11% to $2.7 million, while operating income rose 26% to $1.3 million. Newmarket Village reached 99% retail occupancy, and quarterly percentage rent from third-party tenants increased sequentially.

Russell Index Addition Raises Visibility

Reading was added to the Russell Microcap Index. Management said the inclusion could improve the company’s visibility among institutional investors and funds that track Russell benchmarks.

New York Theater and Leasing Activity

The Orpheum’s Slam Frank opened in September, was extended through January 4, 2027, and received favorable critical comments. Newmark is also discussing leasing opportunities with several significant prospects for the remaining floors at 44 Union Square.

Film Slate Supports Optimism

Management highlighted a broad upcoming slate, including The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Avengers: Doomsday, Dune: Part Two and Jumanji. Longer-term titles mentioned included Avengers: Secret Wars, Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse, Star Wars: Starfighter, Shrek 5, Frozen 3 and The Legend of Zelda.

Cash Balance Remains Limited

Total assets declined to $423.6 million from $434.9 million at the end of 2025, largely because cash was used to fund operations. Cash and cash equivalents stood at $6.1 million on September 30, highlighting Reading’s limited liquidity cushion.

Nine-Month Loss Remains

Despite the major improvement in quarterly results, Reading still reported a $5.4 million net loss for the first nine months. The result shows that the recovery has not yet translated into profitability for the full year.

U.S. Real Estate Weakens

Global real estate revenue fell 6% to $4.3 million, while operating income declined 4% to $1.3 million. U.S. real estate revenue dropped 26% to $1.4 million and produced a $379,000 operating loss.

Australia and New Zealand Occupancy Falls

Combined Australia and New Zealand real estate occupancy declined to 90% from 98% in the prior quarter. The change followed the expiration of two office leases held by one major Newmarket Village tenant, covering about 15,600 square feet.

Live Theater Results Decline

U.S. live theater results were weaker than a year earlier because of longer dark periods at the Minetta Lane and Orpheum Theatres. Minetta Lane hosted only four short productions, while the Orpheum had no performances for most of the quarter.

Attendance and Cost Pressures Persist

Cinema attendance remains below pre-pandemic levels, while labor and utility costs have risen materially. Management said there is limited room to increase ticket and food prices, and operating income has not kept pace with historic rent increases.

Closed Theater Reduces Cash Flow

The closed Cinemas 1, 2 and 3 location will no longer provide annual operating cash flow that historically ranged from several hundred thousand dollars to nearly $1 million. One-time defect costs and legal fees tied to the sale were below $300,000.

Newberry Yard Sale Has No Update

The 23.9-acre Newberry Yard industrial property remains classified as held for sale. Management provided no new information about the sale process during the quarter.

No U.S. Pandemic Assistance

Management said Reading did not receive U.S. government assistance through the shuttered venue grant program. The company therefore did not benefit from that source of pandemic-era support.

STB Appeal Continues

Reading has not received an oral argument date from the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals for its STB case. Management said neither the city nor Center City District has recently made an acquisition proposal or started condemnation proceedings, while legal fees continue.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management expects a strong film lineup in the fourth quarter of 2026 and throughout 2027, while the Board remains focused on reducing debt and preserving Reading’s two-business, three-country strategy. Two U.S. cinema renovations are expected before the end of 2027, and Wellington is targeted for a late-2027 relaunch following a planned February 2027 handover and extensive premium upgrades.

Reading’s call showed a business recovering sharply on stronger films, international cinema performance, premium offerings and disciplined debt actions. Still, limited cash, persistent costs, weaker real estate and theater activity, and a remaining annual loss mean investors will be watching closely for sustained profitability.

data.title: Stem Earnings Call Highlights PowerTrack Growth and Risks
data.description:
Stem, Inc. ((STEM)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Stem’s earnings call presented a mixed but strategically focused picture. Record margins, stronger adjusted EBITDA, positive operating cash flow and PowerTrack growth supported an upbeat tone, although lower revenue, bookings, guidance and ARR, NYSE compliance concerns and a going-concern disclosure kept financial risks in focus.

Record Margins and EBITDA Growth

Stem reported a record third-quarter non-GAAP gross margin of 58%, up from 47% a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $7.1 million, producing a 19% margin and 15% sequential growth.

EBITDA Ahead of Original Plan

Adjusted EBITDA reached $15.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $1.2 million in the same period last year. That result already exceeded the top end of Stem’s original full-year guidance.

Positive Operating Cash Flow

Operating cash flow was positive at $1.5 million in the third quarter. The figure improved by about $1.2 million from the previous quarter, marking progress in cash generation.

PowerTrack Revenue and ARR Advance

PowerTrack software revenue rose 18% year over year to $11 million and increased 12% sequentially. PowerTrack ARR grew 14% year over year and 4% sequentially to approximately $44 million to $44.4 million.

Solar Assets Reach Record Level

Solar assets under management reached a record 40 gigawatts after Stem added 1.7 gigawatts during the quarter. The increase highlights the scale of the company’s monitoring software platform.

PowerTrack Margins Expand

PowerTrack’s non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 80% in the third quarter from 75% in the first half of 2026. Management said the platform continues to deliver double-digit growth while expanding margins.

Leading U.S. C&I Monitoring Position

Stem said PowerTrack remains the leading U.S. commercial and industrial solar monitoring solution. The platform holds an estimated 70% share of that market, giving the company a strong base for software expansion.

Higher-Margin Strategy Takes Priority

Stem is directing more investment toward PowerTrack, its highest-margin and fastest-growing business. It is deemphasizing managed services and battery hardware resale to create a simpler, more software-focused operation.

Athena Intellectual Property Sale

Stem signed an agreement to sell the intellectual property of its Athena storage optimization platform for $10 million in cash. Management said the transaction monetizes technology outside the core business and supports further PowerTrack investment.

Legacy Liabilities Reduced

The company disposed of its economic interest in most consolidated special purpose entities. Stem expects the move to remove nearly $30 million in liabilities, simplify its financial statements and support its exit from managed services.

New Products Win Recognition

Stem launched PowerTrack Sage and PowerTrack EMS during the past year. PowerTrack EMS also received the Smarter E Award for innovation, providing external recognition for the company’s product development.

Net Loss Narrows

Third-quarter net loss improved to $14.6 million from $23.8 million a year earlier. The change reflected higher GAAP gross profit, lower expenses, a $3.2 million gain on energy storage system sales and a $2.9 million impairment tied to the managed-services shift.

Operating Expenses Decline

Cash operating expenses fell 17% year over year and 4% sequentially. Lower personnel and professional service costs drove the reduction while Stem continued funding the PowerTrack platform.

International Utility-Scale Expansion

Stem has booked utility-scale projects in 15 countries and PowerTrack EMS projects in six countries. Boltorov selected the company for the 68-megawatt Marneuli 1 plant in Georgia, which is scheduled for commissioning in the first quarter of 2027.

Copec Partnership Expands in Latin America

Stem entered an agreement with Copec’s renewable-energy subsidiary to deliver storage and energy management solutions, initially in Chile. The relationship includes PowerTrack controls for the 420 megawatt-hour Granja solar battery project, with Colombia and other markets under consideration.

New Ohio Utility Deployment

PowerTrack went live at Border Basin Solar’s 152-megawatt DC project in Hancock County, Ohio. The platform provides plant controls, data acquisition and monitoring for electricity delivered into the PJM market.

Hungary Hybrid Solar Projects

Solarmarkt Group selected Stem’s energy management system to hybridize two operating solar plants in Hungary. The project adds to the company’s international EMS deployment activity.

AIONA AI Services Advance

Stem continued customer discussions around AIONA, its artificial intelligence services offering launched in June. The initial focus is on existing customers and applications that can deliver measurable operational value.

Contracted and Total ARR Grow

Contracted ARR increased 2% sequentially to $70.5 million. Total ARR rose 3% sequentially and 6% year over year to $64 million, while PowerTrack ARR posted stronger growth.

Liquidity and Covenants

Stem ended the quarter with $36.9 million in cash and cash equivalents and did not use its ATM program. Management said the company remained in compliance with its debt covenants and generated positive cash flow in the last two quarters.

Revenue Declines

Third-quarter revenue fell 4% year over year to $36.7 million. Battery hardware resale revenue dropped to $1.4 million from $4.3 million a year earlier, weighing on the total.

Edge Hardware Weakens

Edge hardware revenue declined 11% year over year to $13.8 million. The result reflects softer activity in a business receiving less strategic emphasis than PowerTrack software.

U.S. Solar Bookings Face Delays

U.S. solar bookings fell about 6% sequentially as customers adjusted to the investment tax credit phaseout and changing local regulations. Management said financing changes also delayed construction starts for some projects with 2027 safe-harbor equipment.

Bookings and Backlog Fall

Third-quarter bookings were $27.6 million, down from $36 million in the second quarter and $30 million a year earlier. Contracted backlog declined to $22.3 million from $27.1 million, reflecting weaker domestic solar activity and the exit from lower-priority businesses.

Managed Services Under Review

Managed services historically generated about 45% non-GAAP gross margins, well below PowerTrack’s roughly 75%. Management said these contracts were not accretive, consumed capital and attention, and included significant noncash revenue from legacy financing entities.

Revenue Guidance Reduced

Stem lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $132 million to $142 million from $140 million to $190 million. Battery hardware resale is now expected to contribute up to $2 million, compared with as much as $40 million previously, while managed services and financing entities are being reduced.

Cash Flow Outlook Cut

Operating cash flow guidance was reduced to negative $5 million to positive $5 million from zero to $10 million. The earlier outlook assumed cash collections from battery resales and managed-services activity that Stem no longer expects.

Year-End ARR Guidance Lowered

Stem cut year-end ARR guidance to $50 million to $55 million. Approximately $10 million of current ARR tied to financing entities is expected to be removed in the fourth quarter.

Fourth-Quarter Pressure Expected

Management expects fourth-quarter margins to be slightly lower than in the third quarter. Adjusted EBITDA is also expected to decline because financing-entity revenue will roll off and seasonal factors will weigh on performance.

Managed-Services Revenue Rolls Off

Stem expects about a $3 million reduction in run-rate managed-services revenue during the fourth quarter. The legacy entities currently represent roughly $10 million of ARR and contracted ARR, which the company expects to remove.

Storage Asset Impairment

Stem recorded a $2.9 million impairment on certain energy storage system assets. The charge followed the decision to deemphasize related service offerings.

Storage Assets Remain Flat

Storage operating assets under management were unchanged sequentially at 1.8 gigawatt hours. This contrasts with the growth in solar assets managed through PowerTrack.

Cash Balance Declines

Cash and cash equivalents fell to $36.9 million at the end of the third quarter from $38.4 million at the end of the second quarter. The decline adds importance to the company’s efforts to improve margins and manage capital needs.

NYSE Compliance Notice

Stem received a New York Stock Exchange notice related to market capitalization and stockholders’ equity requirements. Its shares continue to trade on the exchange, and the company plans to submit a compliance plan that could provide 18 months to regain compliance after approval.

Going-Concern Disclosure

Stem’s third-quarter 10-Q included a disclosure about its ability to continue as a going concern within one year. Management said the language was mainly triggered by the existing capital structure and maintained that the company has liquidity to operate in the near term.

Strategic Alternatives Review

The board has begun reviewing strategic alternatives to maximize shareholder value. Outside advisers are assisting with possible business and capital-structure options, but management provided no timeline or additional details.

2026 Guidance Points to a Smaller, Higher-Margin Business

For full-year 2026, Stem expects revenue of $132 million to $142 million, non-GAAP gross margin of 45% to 55% and adjusted EBITDA of $15 million to $20 million. Operating cash flow is expected between negative $5 million and positive $5 million, while year-end ARR is forecast at $50 million to $55 million.

The company also expects lower fourth-quarter margins and EBITDA, a roughly $3 million managed-services revenue roll-off and the removal of about $10 million in financing-related ARR. These targets reflect a deliberate shift away from hardware resale and legacy services toward software revenue.

Stem’s call showed meaningful progress in profitability, cash generation and PowerTrack adoption, but also exposed material revenue and balance-sheet pressures. Investors will likely focus on whether the software strategy can offset weaker bookings, listing risks and the loss of legacy revenue while the strategic review continues.

data.title: Vivos Therapeutics Earnings Call Signals Turnaround Risks
data.description:
Vivos Therapeutics, Inc. ((VVOS)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Vivos Therapeutics’ earnings call struck a cautiously constructive tone. Management highlighted stronger nine-month revenue, cost reductions, referral growth and operational improvements, but the company still faces losses, cash use, limited liquidity, financing needs and Nasdaq listing risks.

Revenue and Gross Profit Growth

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue rose 23% to $16.7 million from $13.6 million. Gross profit also increased 23% to $9.3 million, while gross margin improved to 56% from 55%.

Service Revenue Leads Expansion

Nine-month service revenue jumped 57%, or about $4.4 million, as more patients were treated at the Las Vegas and Henderson centers. The gain more than offset a $1.3 million decline in product revenue.

Sequential Operating Improvement

Management said third-quarter revenue increased from the second quarter, while operating expenses and the operating loss declined. The operating loss improved by $0.8 million, or 18%, to $3.9 million.

Lower Third-Quarter Expenses

General and administrative expenses fell 18% to about $6.5 million, while sales and marketing expenses dropped 48% to roughly $0.2 million. Combined, the two categories were $1.6 million lower than in the prior-year quarter.

More Than $5 Million in Annual Savings

Vivos said labor-force reductions and vendor eliminations or renegotiations have removed more than $5 million in current annual operating costs. Management continues to review additional efficiency measures.

Net Loss Improvement

Third-quarter net loss improved to $2 million from $5.4 million a year earlier. The result included an approximately $2.9 million benefit from reversing a previously recorded Employee Retention Credit liability.

Sleep Center Referrals Rise

Monthly new-patient referrals at the two Sleep and Airway Medicine Centers increased nearly fourfold from May 2026. Management attributed the improvement to closer coordination between sleep diagnosis at Sleep Center of Nevada and treatment at the SAMC centers.

Sleep Center Capacity and Call Handling

Vivos is reorganizing Sleep Center of Nevada with AI-driven clinical and practice-management software, upgraded systems and a new structure. The call center cut staff by more than half, added capacity for over 400 calls per day and handled all calls, including callbacks.

Payer Contracts Offer Revenue Opportunity

The company is renegotiating contracts with nearly all commercial payers and has hired professional negotiators. Management sees a potential annual revenue lift approaching $3.8 million, without higher patient volumes or additional services.

Collections Improve

Vivos engaged a professional medical billing agency to improve collections. Management reported a material reduction in accounts receivable and a six-figure increase in monthly collections from older outstanding balances.

Broader Clinical Services

The company is developing EEG testing, insomnia care, PAP and CPAP distribution and setup, and remote monitoring for CPAP users. These offerings are intended to broaden Vivos’ clinical base beyond obstructive sleep apnea treatment.

South Florida Center Planned

Through its relationship with South Palm Cardiovascular Associates, Vivos plans to establish a Sleep and Airway Medicine Center near one of the group’s four South Florida locations. The practice serves an estimated population of more than 31,000 patients.

SOD Sciences Transaction

On October 16, 2026, Vivos completed a transaction giving it at least an 11% diluted equity interest in SOD Sciences and a 50% co-ownership interest in a pseudohypoxia early-warning test and related intellectual property. The deal involved 12,000 Series C convertible preferred shares and no cash payment.

Debt Exchange Supports Equity Position

Vivos exchanged about $6.1 million of Streeterville Capital senior secured debt for equity. Total liabilities fell to approximately $20.7 million from $26.7 million at the end of 2025, and Nasdaq later confirmed that the company had regained compliance with its stockholders’ equity requirement, subject to monitoring.

FDA-Cleared Treatment Portfolio

Certain Vivos appliances are FDA-cleared for mild to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults. The DNA appliance is also cleared for specified patients ages six through 17 with moderate to severe sleep apnea who require orthodontic treatment.

Third-Quarter Revenue Declines

Third-quarter revenue fell 5% to about $6.4 million from $6.8 million in the prior-year period. Product revenue declined by roughly $0.4 million to $1.8 million as appliance sales to VIPs fell after the company shifted its focus toward sleep centers.

Nine-Month Product Sales Weaken

Product revenue declined approximately $1.3 million during the first nine months of 2026. The reduction reflected lower sales of on-demand orthodontic devices to VIP members following the strategic pivot.

Gross Margin Faces Pressure

Third-quarter gross profit decreased about $0.6 million to $3.3 million. Gross margin fell to 52% from 58%, largely because of the lower contribution from product revenue.

Cost of Sales Increases

Third-quarter cost of sales rose 9% to about $3.1 million, while the nine-month figure increased 22% to $7.4 million. The increases were mainly tied to diagnostic services, patient therapy and added staff at treatment centers.

Center Expansion Raises Year-to-Date Costs

Nine-month general and administrative expenses climbed 17% to $22.5 million as Vivos established its two Sleep and Airway Medicine Centers. Higher salaries, professional fees, occupancy costs and other expenses contributed to the increase.

Depreciation and Interest Expense Rise

Depreciation and amortization increased to $1.5 million from $0.9 million as new assets entered service. Other expense rose $2.3 million year to date, primarily because of interest expense and short-term financing agreements.

Losses and Cash Use Continue

Vivos reported a nine-month net loss of $15.2 million, compared with $14.3 million a year earlier. Operating cash use increased to approximately $12.3 million, and the accumulated deficit reached about $140.5 million.

Limited Cash Creates Going-Concern Risk

Cash and cash equivalents totaled only about $0.2 million at September 30, 2026. Management said that amount would not fund operations and strategic objectives for the next 12 months, creating substantial doubt about the company’s ability to continue without new financing.

Additional Financing Needed

Management said Vivos will need additional financing to meet cash requirements while it works to increase revenue and reach positive operating cash flow. The company also had approximately $2.3 million of principal outstanding under its Streeterville Capital note, due June 10, 2027.

Nasdaq Equity Compliance Remains Conditional

Stockholders’ equity was approximately $2.4 million at September 30, below Nasdaq’s $2.5 million minimum. Although the SOD Sciences transaction helped restore compliance, Nasdaq will continue monitoring the company, and another failure could lead to delisting action.

Minimum Bid Price Risk Persists

Vivos remains below Nasdaq’s $1 minimum bid-price requirement, with a compliance period running through December 4, 2026. The stock has recently traded below $0.10, and shareholders are scheduled to vote on a proposed reverse split intended to address the issue.

Execution Depends on Capital

Management’s plans for clinical services, payer improvements, revenue growth and stronger margins depend on execution, patient participation and favorable payer terms. They also depend on Vivos securing enough capital to operate and develop the business.

SOD Opportunities Remain Uncertain

Potential marketing arrangements involving American Health Associates and Cleveland Clinic Weston Florida still require definitive agreements. Vivos said these possible channels are not being treated as contracted revenue, while accounting for the transaction remains subject to purchase-price allocation and auditor review.

Forward Guidance

Management expects new clinical services and payer initiatives to begin contributing to revenue and margins in the fourth quarter of 2026, with a larger impact during 2027. It also expects payer-rate increases to scale in the first half of 2027, sees potential annual revenue of nearly $3.8 million from contract changes, and targets positive operating cash flow in early 2027.

The call presented evidence of an operating turnaround, especially in service revenue, cost control, referrals and collections. However, severe liquidity constraints, continued losses, financing dependence and Nasdaq bid-price concerns remain central risks for investors.

data.title: Hawthorn Bancshares Amends Chief Executive Officer Employment Agreement
data.description:
Hawthorn Bancshares ( (HWBK) ) has issued an update.

On November 19, 2026, Hawthorn Bancshares and Hawthorn Bank entered into an amended and restated employment agreement with Brent Giles, chief executive officer of both entities, effective that date. The agreement replaced the employment agreement effective May 1, 2023, and established a rolling two-year term, with either side able to give at least 90 days’ non-renewal notice.

Under the agreement, Giles’s minimum annual base salary increased from $450,000 to $500,000 effective January 1, 2026, while incentive and equity eligibility remained. Severance and change-in-control provisions were revised, post-employment non-competition and non-solicitation covenants extended to 18 months, and executive health-examination reimbursement replaced the prior country-club dues benefit; payments remained subject to regulatory limits and applicable conditions.

data.title: BioLineRx Earnings Call Highlights GLIX1 Momentum and Funding
data.description:
Bioline RX Ltd Sponsored ADR ((BLRX)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

BioLineRx’s earnings call struck a broadly positive tone as rapid GLIX1 progress, encouraging cancer data and a stronger funding position outweighed setbacks. Investors also heard caution around a wider net loss, the discontinued CheMo4METPANC study and uncertainty over motixafortide’s future, leaving the company increasingly focused on GLIX1.

GLIX1 Trial Advances Without New Safety Concerns

BioLineRx said GLIX1 dosing has reached the fourth cohort of its Phase I dose-escalation study, which is moving quickly across four leading U.S. cancer centers. No significant treatment-emergent adverse events or other identified safety concerns have been reported so far.

Trial Amendment Adds Valuable Tumor Data

A protocol amendment will allow some patients to receive GLIX1 before planned tumor surgery during the remaining dose-escalation cohorts. This could provide tissue data on brain penetration, biological activity, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, target engagement and survival.

Preclinical GBM Results Show Stronger Effects at Higher Doses

In orthotopic glioblastoma models, GLIX1 produced significant tumor growth inhibition and improved survival, with greater benefits at higher doses. The drug also showed a robust effect in a temozolomide-resistant patient-derived model, while temozolomide produced no meaningful response.

GLIX1 Reaches the Brain and Engages Its Target

New preclinical analyses found that oral GLIX1 reached the brain at every tested dose, with exposure rising at higher doses. Tumor 5hmC levels also increased in a dose-dependent manner and correlated with tumor growth inhibition, supporting evidence of target engagement.

Company Sees Wider Development Potential

BioLineRx highlighted GLIX1’s blood-brain barrier penetration, activity against patient-derived glioma stem cells and strong antitumor effects in animal models. It also pointed to a favorable toxicology profile and the potential to study newly diagnosed or recurrent GBM, as well as other cancers, alone or with standard treatments.

GLIX1 Shows Synergy With Ovarian Cancer Drugs

In a patient-derived model of HR-proficient ovarian cancer, low-dose GLIX1 combined with olaparib performed substantially better than control and monotherapy treatments. Tumor reduction was comparable to cisplatin, while additional testing found reproducible synergy with olaparib, niraparib and veliparib.

Ovarian Cancer Trial Strategy Is Still Taking Shape

The company plans to include an ovarian cancer arm in the Phase IIa expansion, although the specific treatment setting remains under review. BioLineRx is also discussing possible development collaborations with leading PARP inhibitor companies.

GLIX1 Gains Visibility at Major Conferences

GLIX1 research and the clinical trial design were presented at EANO, ESMO and SNO. The EANO preclinical work was selected for a mini oral presentation, while the clinical design appeared in a poster, increasing the program’s visibility among specialists.

Royalty Deal Adds Nondilutive Capital

BioLineRx entered a $5.6 million royalty monetization agreement with Soleus Capital covering its 14.4% net royalty interest in future APHEXDA sales. The proceeds are intended to support GLIX1 development and operating needs, including a partial repayment of the BlackRock loan.

Loan Balance Expected to Fall Sharply

Following the planned repayment, the BlackRock loan balance is expected to decline to about $2 million. The $4 million minimum cash requirement will also be eliminated, while BioLineRx will retain future commercial milestones under its original Ayrmid agreement.

Cash Position Supports Extended Operations

Cash, cash equivalents and short-term bank deposits totaled $12.4 million at September 30, 2026. Including the expected Soleus proceeds, management said available resources should cover projected cash needs into the second half of 2027.

APHEXDA Continues to Generate Royalty Revenue

Ayrmid reported third-quarter APHEXDA sales of $2.4 million, producing approximately $0.4 million in royalty revenue for BioLineRx. The company’s total third-quarter revenue was also $0.4 million, unchanged from the same period in 2025.

Capital Allocation Centers on GLIX1

Management said current capital is being directed primarily toward GLIX1, reflecting the program’s clinical momentum and broader development opportunity. Motixafortide work in solid tumors remains under evaluation while the company reviews additional data.

Potential APHEXDA Milestones Remain in View

The Ayrmid agreement includes roughly $80 million in potential commercial milestones, with some tied to nearer-term events and others linked to higher sales levels. Management said a milestone within the next 12 to 18 months is possible but stressed that it cannot make a commitment.

CheMo4METPANC Study Discontinued for Futility

An interim analysis found that the randomized Phase II CheMo4METPANC trial was unlikely to meet its original objectives, leading BioLineRx to discontinue the study. The company is still reviewing the full data set for potentially positive signals in specific patient subgroups.

Motixafortide’s Next Steps Remain Unclear

BioLineRx is waiting for further pancreatic cancer analyses before deciding how to proceed with motixafortide in PDAC and other solid tumors. Management described the program as being in a wait-and-see phase, although discussions with its Asian partner are continuing.

GLIX1 Investment Drives Higher R&D Spending

Third-quarter research and development expenses rose to $2.7 million from $1.7 million a year earlier, an increase of about 59%. The company attributed most of the $1 million increase to costs associated with the GLIX1 program.

Quarterly Net Loss Expanded Significantly

BioLineRx reported a third-quarter net loss of $3.9 million, compared with a $1.0 million loss in the year-earlier period. The $2.9 million increase reflected higher development spending and a less favorable mix of nonoperating results.

Nonoperating Results Turned Negative

Nonoperating expenses reached $0.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $1.2 million of nonoperating income a year earlier. The latest expense mainly reflected warrant offering costs, while the prior-year income largely came from fair-value adjustments to warrant liabilities.

Financial Results Also Shifted to an Expense

Net financial expense was $0.1 million, versus net financial income of $0.1 million in the comparable quarter. Interest paid on loans was the main cost, partly offset by income from investments.

Investigator Studies Offer Benefits but Less Control

Management described investigator-initiated studies as a double-edged sword for the company. They can broaden research opportunities, but BioLineRx has less control over execution, and these studies typically move more slowly and involve fewer sites than company-sponsored or pharmaceutical-partnered trials.

Guidance Points to GLIX1 Data in 2027

BioLineRx expects the Phase I GLIX1 study to enroll up to 30 patients and continues to target data from that portion in the first half of 2027. The planned Phase IIa expansion is intended to include newly diagnosed and recurrent GBM cohorts, along with other cancers.

The expected $5.6 million Soleus transaction should reduce the remaining loan balance to about $2 million and remove the minimum cash requirement. Management believes cash and other resources can fund operations into the second half of 2027, while a commercial milestone within 12 to 18 months remains possible but uncertain.

BioLineRx left the call with a clear strategic priority: advance GLIX1 while preserving financial flexibility. The program’s early safety profile and preclinical results are encouraging, but investors must balance that promise against rising costs, the failed pancreatic study and unresolved questions surrounding motixafortide.

data.title: Carclo Earnings Call Highlights Stronger Profit and Returns
data.description:
Carclo plc ((GB:CAR)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Carclo’s earnings call carried a strongly positive tone, with management highlighting higher profit, stronger cash generation, improved margins and better returns despite lower revenue. The main concerns were weaker Diagnostics demand, raw material inflation, pension obligations, customer concentration and the continued absence of a dividend, but operational progress outweighed these challenges.

Profit Rose Despite Revenue Decline

Underlying profit increased 21.8% to £6.7 million even as revenue fell 3.1% to £55.5 million. Management credited self-help measures, tighter cost control, improved revenue quality and a reshaped portfolio for the stronger result.

Cash Generation More Than Doubled

Cash generated from operations more than doubled to £7.9 million, while underlying EBITDA reached £9.7 million. Cash conversion improved to 81.9%, supported by active management of inventory and receivables.

Margins and Earnings Per Share Improved

Underlying earnings per share rose to 3p from 0.9p, while the operating margin reached 12.1%. The improvement reflected stronger divisional trading and lower central costs.

Returns Beat Precision 2030 Minimums

Trailing 12-month return on sales reached 12.3%, above the 10% minimum target, while return on capital employed rose to 29.1%, exceeding the 25% goal. Net debt excluding leases stood at £17.9 million, and the Board said full-year profit and cash generation remained on track.

Long-Term Return on Sales Progress

Return on sales has climbed steadily from 3.2% three years ago to 12.3%. Management attributed the progress to a focus on regulated, non-commoditized markets, a higher-return portfolio and improved operating efficiency.

Specialty Delivered Strong Growth

Specialty revenue increased 12.1% to £8.9 million, while underlying operating profit grew by more than 35% to £2.3 million. Its margin expanded to 26.1% from 21.6%, helped by operating leverage and a favorable product mix.

Aerospace Demand Remained Robust

Strong Aerospace demand supported Specialty’s performance, with Carclo securing two significant new customers that are Tier 1 suppliers to aircraft manufacturers. Overall Aerospace sales have nearly tripled since financial year 2022.

Manufacturing Capability Expanded

Carclo increased machining capability in France, strengthening its ability to serve Aerospace customers. Its Indian operations also achieved full manufacturing and assembly AS9100 certification, a key quality standard for the sector.

CTP Protected Profitability

CTP revenue fell 5.6% to £46.5 million, but underlying profit was almost unchanged at £6.7 million. The division’s margin increased to 14.5% from 13.8%, remaining comfortably above its 10% return objective.

Diagnostics Volumes Began to Recover

Diagnostics volumes improved in the second quarter after a weaker first quarter, offering some relief within CTP. Management said two projects for new customers in new sectors had passed qualification testing and were moving toward production.

New Customers and Proposals Increased

Carclo won new customers in both divisions, including accounts in newer market sectors and new routes to market. The company also strengthened its commercial team, contributing to increased proposal activity.

Earlier Customer Design Involvement

The group is moving earlier into customers’ design processes through its commercial and design engineering teams, supported by the Innovation Center in Czechia. Management said this capability helps guide customers from initial design through validated production.

Bank Debt and Pension Exposure Fell

Net cash from operating activities increased to £4.1 million from £0.4 million, helping reduce net debt excluding leases to £17.9 million, or 0.9 times trailing 12-month EBITDA. Net debt and the pension deficit together were described as almost one-third lower than the £112 million reported in financial year 2022.

Pension Burden Became More Manageable

The technical provisions pension deficit declined to £49.6 million from £52.9 million at March, while the IAS 19 accounting liability fell by £4.7 million to £42.1 million. Pension cash costs now equal 18% of EBITDA, down from 30% in financial year 2022.

Financial Resilience Improved

The incident frequency rate improved from 2.7 to 0.4, while net debt to EBITDA including leases fell from 2.5 times to 1.3 times. Over the same period, return on sales rose from 4.7% to 12.3% and return on capital employed increased from 6.1% to 29.1%.

India Added Diversification

Carclo expanded Life Sciences capacity in India, gained two Life Sciences customers and began work on a larger programme. The facility has moved from dependence on one product to multiple products, with further opportunities in Life Sciences and Aerospace.

Investment Took Priority Over Dividends

The Board chose to invest in profitable growth rather than pay a dividend for the half. Spending is continuing on machining, Life Sciences capacity, customer design capabilities and other opportunities linked to the Precision 2030 plan.

Revenue Decline Reflected Diagnostics Weakness

Group revenue decreased 3.1% to £55.5 million, mainly because of softer Diagnostics demand. CTP Manufacturing Solutions revenue was reduced by £2.6 million, with weakness particularly evident in the U.S. and China.

Raw Material Costs Created Pressure

CTP faced higher raw material prices during the half, adding pressure to the division’s cost base. Even so, its margin improved as management controlled costs and protected the quality of revenue.

Pension Deficit Remains Significant

Management stressed that the pension scheme deficit remains a substantial financial commitment. The technical provisions deficit was £49.6 million and the IAS 19 accounting liability stood at £42.1 million.

Leases Lifted Reported Net Debt

Net debt including leases was £26.2 million, or 1.3 times EBITDA, compared with £17.9 million, or 0.9 times EBITDA, excluding leases. The difference followed the renewal of the Greensburg facility lease during the period.

No Near-Term Dividend Planned

Management said the Board would continue prioritizing investment in profitable growth over shareholder distributions. Dividends are not expected to return in the short term or near horizon.

Customer Concentration Remains a Risk

A significant share of revenue comes from a small number of large customers, creating an area of investor risk. Management described these relationships as close and long term while emphasizing efforts to broaden the customer base.

Regulated Growth Takes Time

Carclo noted that growth in regulated markets requires lengthy development and approval processes. In CTP, as much as 18 months can pass before manufacturing revenue begins after design, tooling and validation.

Guidance and Precision 2030 Targets

The Board reaffirmed its expectations for full-year profit and cash generation, while CTP expects improved volumes to continue in the second half. Two new customer projects are expected to enter production during the financial year, with Precision 2030 targeting at least 10% return on sales, 25% return on capital employed, net debt below 0.5 times EBITDA by financial year 2031 and organic revenue growth above 8% annually over the plan.

Carclo’s call presented a business with stronger profitability, cash flow and returns despite a revenue setback in Diagnostics. Investment, new customers and Aerospace momentum support the longer-term case, although pension commitments, customer concentration and the lack of a near-term dividend remain important considerations for investors.

data.title: ALS Earnings Call Signals Strong Growth Despite Life Sciences Weakness
data.description:
ALS Ltd. ((AU:ALQ)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

ALS delivered a strong first half, with revenue, earnings, margins, returns and liquidity all improving. The upbeat performance was led by Commodities and Minerals, although weaker Life Sciences results, cost pressures, foreign exchange and softer cash conversion tempered the picture.

Strong First-Half Financial Performance

ALS reported revenue of $1.72 billion, up 10.2% organically. Underlying EBIT rose 18.6% to $332.7 million, while underlying NPAT increased 23.6% to a record $214.6 million and underlying EPS climbed 21.6% to $0.423.

Returns and Margins Improved

Return on capital employed increased 233 basis points to 21.1%, despite higher investment in growth. Organic expansion, better business mix, lower corporate costs and a favorable 30-basis-point foreign-exchange effect lifted the group margin by 250 basis points to 19.4%.

Commodities Delivered Strong Growth

Commodities organic revenue rose 24.5%, or 26.1% at constant currency, while EBIT increased 42.7% on the same basis. Margin reached 31.6%, supported by strong volumes, pricing discipline, favorable mix, cost control and the hub-and-spoke operating model.

Minerals Reached Record Levels

Minerals organic revenue increased 30.4%, with EBIT margin expanding 350 basis points to 34.7%. Higher sample volumes, disciplined pricing, favorable mix and cost control supported the result, while exploration demand remained strong across major mining regions.

Metallurgy and Mine Sites Expanded

Metallurgy achieved about 20% organic revenue growth and improved margins. Mine-site revenue also grew at a double-digit rate, supported by new project wins, with two or three sites under construction and further organic and acquisition opportunities being assessed.

Geochemistry Demand Stayed Healthy

Sample volumes remained solid, with major and mid-tier customers accounting for about 72% of volumes and juniors representing 28%. Year-to-date drill projects rose 13% for gold and 38% for specialty commodities, although October activity fell 4% month on month after a strong September.

New Testing Methods Gained Ground

Revenue from newer high-performance methods and downstream services increased to $52 million from $22 million over four years. The roughly 33% compound annual growth rate reflects ALS’s expanding role across the mining value chain and its ability to serve both existing and new customers.

Food and Non-U.S. Environmental Businesses Grew

Food posted 6.8% organic growth, marking its fourth consecutive year of expansion, while margin rose 40 basis points. Environmental outside the United States grew 3.8%, led by APAC, EMEA and Canada, and PFAS revenue rose about 14% to roughly 6% of environmental revenue.

Balance Sheet Supported Shareholder Returns

Leverage stood at 1.5 times, below the targeted 1.7-to-2.3-times range, with more than $430 million of available liquidity and interest cover of 15.6 times. The board declared an interim dividend of $0.233 per share, about 20% above the prior period, representing a payout of roughly 55% of underlying NPAT.

Hub-Lab Investment Progressed

Capital expenditure totaled $152 million, including $34 million for hub labs and $118 million of base spending. The Smithfield hub in Sydney and Lima hub in Peru opened on time and on budget, while Thailand remained on schedule for commissioning in mid-2027 and ALS explored an earlier completion for Prague.

Technology and Automation Programs Advanced

ALS moved its Lab of the Future program from pilot to broader deployment, with about 30% of employees using generative artificial intelligence in their daily work. Investment continued in data governance, digital efficiency, innovation, automation and infrastructure, with management expecting these initiatives to reach a profitable run rate by the end of fiscal 2027.

Safety Performance Improved

Management reported continued improvement in safety across ALS laboratories and sites worldwide. Visible leadership, stronger risk management and employee engagement were credited with supporting the progress.

Life Sciences Missed Expectations

Life Sciences delivered only 1.8% organic revenue growth, while constant-currency EBIT was $141.9 million and margin was 13.6%. Reported margin fell 95 basis points to 13.7%, mainly because of weaker U.S. Environmental and Pharma results, particularly at Nuvisan in Europe.

U.S. Environmental Lost Revenue and Clients

U.S. Environmental faced a difficult market and reported an organic revenue decline. Although quality and compliance matters were resolved with regulators, ALS lost some clients and capacity, while projects not won in the first half will not return later in the year.

Nuvisan Orders Converted More Slowly

Nuvisan revenue declined as European early-stage pharmaceutical outsourcing slowed and its largest customer reduced activity. The order book remains in place, but customer budgets delayed conversion, while the anchor client’s share of revenue fell from about 40% to roughly one-third.

Life Sciences Recovery Will Take Time

Nuvisan improved in the second quarter but remained below management’s expectations. Further efficiency measures are planned, although management said returning Life Sciences to neutral full-year margin performance may be beyond reach, with larger benefits expected in later years.

Oil and Lubricants Activity Softened

Oil and Lubricants performance weakened as customers reduced activity and lubricant supply tightened. ALS is prioritizing the consolidation of its expanded greenfield network and seeking higher utilization across the business.

Wage and Logistics Costs Pressured Margins

Management said wage and logistics inflation had started to weigh on Minerals margins. The company is managing the pressures through cost control, pricing discipline and operational improvements.

Foreign Exchange Reduced Reported Growth

A stronger Australian dollar cut reported revenue by $103 million and EBIT by about $15 million. Reported revenue growth was 3.4%, compared with 9.6% on a constant-currency basis, highlighting the significance of currency translation for investors.

Cash Conversion Fell Below Target

EBITDA cash conversion was 82%, below the company’s long-term threshold. ALS increased inventory to manage supply risks linked to the Middle East conflict, while tighter vendor payment terms reduced days payable outstanding.

Middle East Conflict Raised Costs

The conflict increased spending on fuel, freight and consumables such as helium, with about 80% of the roughly $5 million impact occurring in Minerals. Management said the costs were being managed and would be recovered from the market over time.

Commodity and Seasonal Visibility Was Limited

Management said visibility was good for the next three months and possibly six months, but less certain beyond that. Commodity growth rates face tougher comparisons, while a colder North American winter could shift volumes from the fourth quarter into the first quarter.

M&A and Quality Controls Were Strengthened

ALS acknowledged lessons from the York acquisition and said the experience produced a stronger integration playbook. New U.S. quality roles and a global quality-lead position were also created after the Environmental issues, as regulatory standards continue to tighten.

Corporate Costs Are Rising

Corporate costs were $34 million in the first half, or about 2% of revenue. Management expects the ratio to rise as spending timing normalizes and growth investments continue, with cybersecurity investment also increasing after an earlier cyber incident.

Second-Half Guidance Remains Constructive

ALS is targeting high single-digit organic revenue growth and margin expansion at group level in the second half. Minerals is expected to deliver about 20% organic growth for fiscal 2027, roughly 3% scope growth and a further 20-to-30-basis-point margin improvement in the second half.

Life Sciences and Other Guidance

Life Sciences is expected to return to mid-single-digit organic growth in the second half, producing about 3% growth for fiscal 2027 and 40-to-60-basis-point margin improvement. Industrial Materials is expected to post low single-digit growth with stable margins, while base capital expenditure should be $90 million to $100 million in the second half, plus $35 million for hub labs.

Capital Allocation and Financial Targets

ALS is targeting fiscal 2027 EBITDA cash conversion of at least 90%, with stronger performance expected in the second half. Net underlying interest costs are forecast at $68 million to $70 million, corporate costs at about 2.1% of revenue, and each 1% currency movement is expected to affect annual underlying EBIT by about $3.5 million.

ALS entered the period with strong earnings momentum, led by its Commodities and Minerals operations, expanding margins and a healthy balance sheet. The main risks are the slower Life Sciences recovery, cost and currency pressures, softer cash conversion and uncertain market conditions, but management’s outlook remains broadly constructive.

data.title: Zepp Health Earnings Call Signals Recovery Ahead
data.description:
Zepp Health Corporation ((ZEPP)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Zepp Health’s earnings call struck a cautiously optimistic tone. Third-quarter revenue, margins and operating losses weakened year over year, while supply shortages and rising component costs weighed on results. Still, stronger product activations, improving availability, retail expansion and a more positive fourth-quarter outlook suggested that management believes the toughest period is passing.

Sequential Growth and Q4 Outlook

Third-quarter revenue reached $68.3 million, up 7.5% from the second quarter and within the company’s previous guidance range. Management pointed to a stronger fourth quarter, supported by holiday demand and improved product availability.

Balance Activations Accelerate

Global activations for Balance 2, Balance 3, Balance 3 Titanium and Balance Ultra rose about 43% sequentially. Newer, higher-priced models drove the increase, with Balance 3 Titanium representing a growing portion of activations.

Active Series Gains Momentum

Combined activations for Active 3 Premium and Active Max increased about 37% from the second quarter. Management said the broader Active family grew more than 40% sequentially, with momentum continuing into the fourth quarter and holiday season.

Bip Family Preserves Its Scale

Supply of the $79 Bip 6 remained tight during the quarter, but the $99 Bip Max more than offset the decline in Bip 6 activations. Combined activations for the two models were slightly higher than a year earlier.

Premium Outdoor Portfolio Expands

Zepp launched the T-Rex Dual Solar at about $650, extending its premium outdoor lineup. The watch features front-and-back solar charging and offline navigation aimed at supporting multi-day outdoor trips.

Software and Training Features Broaden

Zepp OS 6 reached existing devices including Balance 2, Active Max and T-Rex Pro. New capabilities include training calendars, HybridCharge, training-load and recovery tools, lactate-threshold estimates, route previews, offline maps and expanded HYROX analysis.

Athlete Results Support Cheetah Watches

The company highlighted results from athletes using its Cheetah watches after the quarter. Rose Clark won the Women’s Diagonale des Fous wearing a Cheetah 2 Ultra, while Yemaneberhan Crippa finished second at the New York City Marathon with a Cheetah 2 Pro.

Product Availability Improves

Management said T-Rex 3 and Helio Strap inventory was replenished in the fourth quarter and was well stocked across key markets. The improvement should help Zepp capture more holiday demand after earlier supply limitations.

U.S. Retail Presence Grows

Zepp continued expanding through Best Buy and REI. In selected Best Buy stores, larger screens at Amazfit counters are helping shoppers compare products and understand their activity, training and recovery applications.

Underlying Gross Margin Shows Progress

Reported gross margin declined year over year, but management said normalized margin improved sequentially after excluding a tariff-related benefit in the second quarter. Better product mix offset a meaningful portion of foreign-exchange and component-cost pressure.

Operating Expense Discipline Emerges

Adjusted operating expenses were about $34.2 million, down from $34.8 million in the second quarter. General and administrative expenses fell to $5.6 million, and management expects broader cost-structure improvements to moderate expenses.

Innovation and AI Investment Continues

Research and development spending was $10.7 million, broadly stable from both the prior quarter and the year-earlier period. Zepp continued investing in products, proprietary technology, software, AI capabilities and its wider wearable ecosystem while emphasizing development efficiency.

Inventory Position Improves

Inventory stood at $68.6 million at the end of September, down from $87.7 million a year earlier. Management said the change reflected better alignment among procurement, manufacturing, product availability and market demand.

Debt Profile Strengthens

Zepp converted another $26.6 million of short-term borrowing into long-term obligations during the quarter, taking the year-to-date total to $56.5 million. Cumulative debt retirement since the start of 2023 reached approximately $38.1 million.

Share Repurchase Authorization Extended

The company had used about $17.8 million of its $20 million repurchase authorization by September. The board approved a one-year extension of the existing program, preserving flexibility to continue buying shares.

Free App Strategy Builds the Ecosystem

Zepp currently offers selected app features for free, including food-photo calorie analysis and coaching guidance, to attract users to the Amazfit ecosystem. Management said subscriptions could be considered after the installed base becomes sufficiently large, but not immediately.

Revenue Still Below Last Year

Despite the sequential improvement, third-quarter revenue declined 9.9% from the same period a year earlier to $68.3 million. The result underscored the gap between improving product momentum and the company’s still-challenging annual comparison.

Gross Margin Contracts

Third-quarter gross margin was 35%, compared with 37.4% in the second quarter and 38.2% a year earlier. Higher component costs, foreign exchange and supply pressures offset benefits from product mix.

Supply Shortages Limit Demand Capture

Tight supply for Balance 3, Helio Strap, Bip 6 and T-Rex 3 restricted Zepp’s ability to fully meet demand. Memory-chip lead times also stretched to six or seven months from the normal three to four months.

Balance Ultra Production Stabilizes

Scaling the titanium-alloy midframe for Balance Ultra was a significant manufacturing challenge. Management said the issue was being resolved as production stabilized.

Currency and Component Costs Weigh

The stronger renminbi against the U.S. dollar increased dollar-denominated operating and product costs. Memory-chip inflation, supply constraints and production priorities across the industry added further pressure to component pricing.

Marketing Spending Raises Expenses

Adjusted operating expenses rose to about $34.2 million from $28.6 million a year earlier, led by selling and marketing costs of roughly $18 million. Spending included channel investments, product launches, sports sponsorships and HYROX and New Athlete partnerships.

Operating Loss Widens Year Over Year

The operating loss was $10.3 million, about $1 million narrower sequentially but $10.7 million wider than a year earlier. Management cited higher marketing costs, foreign exchange and component expenses, partly offset by $1.1 million in G&A savings.

Cash Balance Declines

Cash ended the quarter at $99 million, down from $106 million in the second quarter and $102 million a year earlier. Management attributed the sequential decrease mainly to losses incurred during the period.

Competitive Environment Remains Difficult

Management described consumer electronics as challenging and highly competitive, with inflation and economic uncertainty making shoppers more selective. Physical-retail expansion also created a timing gap between initial investment, inventory deployment and eventual revenue contribution.

Fourth-Quarter Guidance and Priorities

Zepp expects fourth-quarter revenue of $90 million to $95 million, representing roughly 6% to 12% year-over-year growth. The company expects supply constraints to ease, gross margin to improve, operating expenses to moderate and marketing spending to decline from second- and third-quarter levels, while it continues extending debt maturities.

Zepp’s call balanced near-term financial pressure with signs of improving execution. Stronger activations, better inventory and retail reach support the recovery case, but margins, cash usage, competition and component costs remain important risks for investors to monitor.

data.title: Vivani Medical Highlights Positive Results for Semaglutide Implant
data.description:
Vivani Medical ( (VANI) ) has provided an update.

On Nov. 23, 2026, Vivani Medical published frequently asked questions about positive top-line results from SLIM-1, the first human study of NPM-139, its investigational semaglutide implant for chronic weight management. The FAQ addressed the study’s tolerability findings, drug levels, weight change, comparison with preclinical results and implications for the planned SLIM-2 trial.

In the four-week, open-label study, 10 participants received low-dose NPM-139 and 10 received weekly Wegovy at its 0.25-mg starting dose. No implant recipients had treatment-related adverse events, compared with mild, gastrointestinal treatment-related events in five Wegovy recipients; neither group had serious adverse events. Mean weight loss was 0.79% with NPM-139 and 0.82% with Wegovy, while drug levels rose gradually in the implant group. Vivani said the findings provided an initial human basis for advancing NPM-139, although longer-duration delivery and weight maintenance had not been established in humans.

data.title: Pinterest Amends Executive Severance and Equity Arrangements
data.description:
Pinterest ( (PINS) ) has shared an announcement.

On November 18, 2026, Pinterest’s Talent Development and Compensation Committee further amended and restated the Severance and Change in Control Plan for employees in Level 21 positions. Subject to a participant signing a separation and release agreement and continuing to comply with confidentiality and invention-assignment terms, outstanding PSUs will vest at the greater of target or actual performance measured at a change in control in specified termination or award non-assumption circumstances.

The plan also states that equity and annual-bonus treatment applies notwithstanding contrary award or program provisions, clarifies awards when no plan benefits apply, and treats certain executives as participants solely for bonus and PSU provisions. The Committee also approved amended and restated agreements for CEO William Ready and Chief Legal and Business Affairs Officer and Corporate Secretary Wanji Walcott, entitling them to annual bonus payments and PSU treatment under the plan, subject to its terms.

The agreements provided that more favorable definitions of “cause” and “good reason” would apply, while Ready’s agreement treated a resignation for good reason outside a change in control as a termination without cause for annual-bonus purposes. The Committee also amended Ready’s PSU awards so, subject to a release, such a resignation would receive the same treatment as a termination without cause, with a prorated portion remaining eligible to vest based on actual performance through the applicable performance period.

data.title: Kairos Pharma Approves Executive Equity Grants and Bylaw Amendments
data.description:
An announcement from Kairos Pharma, Ltd. ( (KAPA) ) is now available.

On November 19, 2026, Kairos Pharma’s Compensation Committee approved an aggregate of 816,335 restricted stock units for certain executive officers under its 2023 Equity Incentive Plan. John S. Yu received 400,000, Neil Bhomick 200,000, Ramachandran Murali 16,335 and Doug Samuelson 200,000; each unit represented the right to receive one common share upon vesting and vested immediately upon issuance.

The grants were made in recognition of the officers’ services and to further align their interests with shareholders. The Board also approved an amendment and restatement of the bylaws on November 19, 2026, reducing the quorum required for a stockholders’ meeting from a majority of votes entitled to be cast to one-third; the amended bylaws became effective immediately after Board approval.
